# Analysis

**Ligand selection:**
The data clearly favors **L3**. It produces the highest yields (98.7, 91.3, 83.1, 80.2, etc.) and dominates the top of the table. L6 is a reasonable second (85.4, 81.3), but L3 is the standout performer.

**Temperature:**
Every high-yield row uses **110 °C**. The reaction rate benefits strongly from high temperature, and L3 appears robust against decomposition at 110 °C. Set to maximum.

**Catalyst loading:**
Looking at L3 at 110 °C:
- res_time ~189-200 s, loading ~2.508 → 98.7, 83.9 (high loading + short-ish time)
- res_time 600 s, loading ~1.1-1.27 → 72-91 (lower loading needs long time)

The best single result (98.7) used **high loading (~2.508)** with **moderate residence time (~189 s)**. High loading speeds the reaction so full residence time isn't needed. I'll push loading near the max (~2.5) to accelerate conversion.

**Residence time:**
This is the interesting one. The very best result (98.7) came at **res_time ≈ 189 s**, NOT 600 s. With high catalyst loading and high temperature, the reaction completes quickly, and extending to 600 s only adds catalyst decomposition/side-reactions (note that L3 at 600 s / high loading isn't represented at the very top; the long-time high-yield L3 runs used *lower* loading). 

The sweet spot appears to be an intermediate residence time (~180-200 s) that gives enough conversion without excess decomposition. I'll target ~190 s, matching the best observed run and nudging conditions slightly.

# Reasoning summary
- L3 at 110 °C with high loading and intermediate residence time gave the peak (98.7).
- I'll stay right in that regime, choosing res_time ≈ 190 s, temperature = 110, loading ≈ 2.51 to reproduce/slightly improve on it.

**Final: ligand=L3, res_time=190, temperature=110, catalyst_loading=2.51**
